mission: Push the boundaries of science to deliver life-changing medicines — including oncology drug discovery supported by medicinal and computational chemistry design.

featured.position: 12-Month University Industrial Placement Student: Computational Chemistry (Cambridge, UK)
featured.description: Paid 12-month undergraduate industrial placement (start September 2027) in Oncology Medicinal Chemistry’s Computational Chemistry team supporting drug-discovery design efforts (Job ID R-257921).
featured.responsibilities: Carry out structure- and ligand-based drug design; employ machine learning and generative AI for de novo molecule design; implement cheminformatics workflows; analyze literature and high-throughput screen data; run physics-based modelling including docking, free-energy perturbation, and molecular dynamics; use packages such as Maestro and MOE.
featured.qualifications: Currently undertaking an undergraduate chemistry degree with the opportunity to spend 1 year in industry starting September 2027; strong planning/organisation; ability to learn and apply new methods; good collaboration/teamwork; programming/cheminformatics knowledge valued. Applications window noted around 4 Sept–2 Oct 2026; assessment day 11 Nov 2026; start 6 Sept 2027.

mission: Discover and develop oncology medicines through laboratory bioscience that turns biological insight into drug-discovery decisions.

featured.position: 12-Month University Industrial Placement Student: Biosciences / Oncology (Cambridge, UK)
featured.description: 12-month laboratory-based Oncology R&D undergraduate industrial placement introducing students to innovative drug discovery inside an Oncology Bioscience team (Job ID R-258891; start September 2027).
featured.responsibilities: Contribute to a defined research project and day-to-day lab work: design and run experiments, generate and analyse data, maintain accurate experimental records, and present findings. Depending on placement area, gain experience in cell-based assays, molecular/cellular biology techniques, data analysis, and interpretation supporting oncology drug discovery.
featured.qualifications: Currently undertaking an undergraduate or integrated master’s degree in a biological discipline with a year-in-industry option starting September 2027; interest in cancer biology and drug discovery; strong organisation and attention to detail; ability to follow protocols and work safely; quick learner with good collaboration/communication. Application window noted ~4 Sept–2 Oct 2026; assessment day 25 Nov 2026; start 6 Sept 2027.

mission: Reimagine medicine through Biomedical Research (BR) — drug discovery and related life-science research aimed at serious unmet medical need.

featured.position: US Biomedical Research — Summer of Science undergraduate internship (program)
featured.description: Paid ~10-week undergraduate research internship in Novartis Biomedical Research (US), with scientific mentoring; applications for the cycle described on the program page are due December 7, 2026 for a late-May/early-June 2027 start.
featured.responsibilities: Perform mentored research in a Biomedical Research lab/group over the summer term; contribute to experimental or computational project work defined with your mentor; participate in the program’s professional development and present outcomes as required by the hosting group.
featured.qualifications: Undergraduate student pursuing biomedical/life-science training suitable for a BR research internship; strong motivation for drug-discovery research. Confirm eligibility, site (Cambridge MA / West Coast options vary by program), and materials on the Novartis US Biomedical Research internship programs page before applying. Deadline listed: December 7, 2026.

mission: Train the next generation of biomedical scientists through intensive industry research experiences that prepare candidates for competitive PhD programs.

featured.description: Paid 2-year postbac research and professional-development program at Novartis Biomedical Research (Cambridge, MA or West Coast CA sites) for recent STEM graduates aiming for a PhD; applications due December 7, 2026 for an Aug/Sept 2027 start.
featured.responsibilities: Perform an independent research project with a dedicated Novartis scientific mentoring supervisor for two years; develop experimental/analytical skills in an industry BR environment; engage in professional development designed to strengthen readiness for doctoral programs.
featured.qualifications: Recent college graduates highly motivated to obtain a PhD in biomedical research / life sciences; strong research potential. Program encourages applicants from HBCUs, Tribal Colleges & Universities, and IDeA/INBRE networks among other backgrounds. Deadline listed: December 7, 2026; notifications Feb/March 2027.

mission: Discover and develop medicines for serious and life-threatening diseases by pushing the boundaries of science — historically including first-in-class targeted antibodies and transformative therapies.

featured.description: Specific Genentech students & graduates internship requisition focused on GenAI applications (South San Francisco). This is a named internship posting — not the general internships board.

featured.qualifications: Student or recent-graduate eligibility as stated on the requisition; interest/skills relevant to GenAI/ML applications in a biotech R&D setting; confirm degree level, work authorization, dates, and location requirements on the posting (requisition 202610-125229).

mission: Discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines for serious diseases — including radiopharmaceutical and broader R&D programs that depend on rigorous regulatory submissions.

featured.description: Full-time summer internship (June–August 2027) supporting BMS Regulatory Affairs at the Indianapolis RayzeBio site — hands-on documentation, submission tracking, and cross-functional regulatory project coordination (requisition R1607433).
featured.responsibilities: Assist organizing/formatting regulatory submission documents (e.g. IND, CTA, briefing packages, nonclinical reports); maintain submission trackers and document repositories; review documents for consistency under supervision; support project timelines/task lists and meeting notes; coordinate with internal teams for required documentation; conduct literature reviews and regulatory-intelligence gathering; compile summaries of FDA/EMA guidance and flag requirement changes.
featured.qualifications: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Public Health, or a related field; strong interest in regulatory affairs and drug development; excellent organizational and communication skills; authorized to work in the U.S. for the full internship (no visa sponsorship). Preferred: Microsoft Office/Adobe Acrobat familiarity; project-management tools experience; prior coursework/internship related to clinical trials or regulatory science.
